title: Chapter 31 — The Write-Up and Transition to Close
intro: Reading readiness, the write-up mechanics, and the post-signature minutes that build the relationship.

sections.title: Reading Readiness
sections.content:
Before you start writing up the sale, you need to know the customer is ready. Jumping to the write-up too early feels presumptuous. Waiting too long lets momentum die.

Buying signals include: asking about delivery dates, asking about financing, asking about warranty, asking about accessories, touching the product repeatedly, discussing where it will go in their home, agreeing with your recommendations throughout the presentation.

When you see multiple buying signals, the customer is ready — even if they have not said 'I want to buy it.' That is your cue to move to Step 9.

sections.title: The Write-Up Process
sections.content:
The write-up should feel like a natural continuation of the conversation — not a sudden shift to paperwork.

Review the complete ticket one more time. Confirm the product, the price, the delivery date, the installation plan, the protection coverage, and any accessories. Make sure there are no surprises.

Then start the order. Be efficient but not rushed. Explain each step of the paperwork. Make the customer feel like they are making a smart decision — because they are.

sections.title: The Post-Signature Moment
sections.content:
What you do after the customer signs matters more than most people realize.

This is the reassurance stage. The customer just committed to a significant purchase. They may feel excited, nervous, or both.

Reassure them. 'Excellent choice. You are going to love this.' Explain the next steps clearly — when delivery will happen, what to expect, who to call if they have questions.

Give them your contact information personally. Not a business card tossed on the counter — a genuine offer. 'Here is my direct number. If anything comes up between now and delivery, call me directly.'

That moment builds the relationship that leads to referrals, repeat business, and a five-star review.

sections.title: Coaching Rule
sections.content:
When evaluating the write-up and transition, ask:

Does the salesperson read buying signals accurately — or move to close too early or too late?
Do they review the complete ticket before starting paperwork?
Is the write-up process smooth and professional?
Do they reassure the customer after the commitment?
Do they provide clear next steps and personal contact information?

The sale is not over when the customer signs. It is over when the customer leaves feeling confident about their decision. That is the moment that generates the review, the referral, and the return visit.
